note: THE LEGEND, correcting its OWN spec after The Pavement challenged it. VERIFIED AT THE SOURCE: decision 0287 decides that a tile at rung d is a facet at depth d and that zooming out truncates the path rather than averaging the picture. Grepped the whole record for vertex, vertices and corner: ZERO MATCHES. Facet-corner-is-a-geosphere-vertex is a corollary of the ICOSPHERE IMPLEMENTATION, not a claim 0287 makes. 0287 therefore survives a square facet untouched and is owed an amendment, not a supersession. The Pavement had this right and I checked rather than conceded. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LEGEND SPEC 3.0, now corrected and committed: I ruled against the game plate fetching scene/tiles-region/v1 on TWO grounds, double-resampling breaking 0287 and 0196 forbidding invented detail below the datum. Both legs are weaker than written. The first is CONTINGENT — it exists only because two meshes exist, and unifying them removes it. The second NEVER APPLIED to the field this campaign added: region.rs line 235 says continuous layers are barycentric and DISCRETE layers are nearest-vertex, and relief is discrete and nearest-vertex by construction at region.rs line 431, so 0196 never bit for it. I had a two-legged argument in which one leg was contingent and the other did not apply to the subject. WHAT SURVIVES IS THINNER AND THE SPEC NOW SAYS SO: the TUI is a Rust client that can call the classifier directly, so a fetch buys a serialization round trip and nothing else. That is simplicity, not correctness. If the cube-sphere lands, share-a-function-not-a-fetch becomes a PREFERENCE rather than a prohibition, and a future campaign moving the plate onto the wire would violate nothing. Recording this because a record that outlives its subject produces wrong answers from readers acting in good faith, which is the sentence The Legend spec opens with, and this was an instance of it in The Legend own spec.
